narrative.intro: Granite Construction has $562M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Granite Construction has 11 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $51.1M. Granite Construction obligations are up 133.9% year over year. Granite Construction received most obligations from the Department of Homeland Security, which obligated $537M. Granite Construction also has obligations from the Department of Defense totaling $13.4M and the Department of Transportation totaling $11.7M. Granite Construction work is concentrated in Commercial and Institutional Building Construction at $537M, with additional activity in Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction at $13.1M and Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction at $11.8M. Granite Construction obligations by fiscal year show growth from earlier years: FY21 at $20.3M, FY22 at $19.7M, FY23 at $335M, FY24 at $185M, FY25 at $240M, and FY26 at $562M.

sections.heading: How has Granite Construction's federal business changed recently?
sections.body: Granite Construction obligations are up 133.9% year over year. Granite Construction has $562M in obligations in FY2026 to date, compared with FY25 obligations of $240M and FY24 obligations of $185M. Granite Construction increased award activity to 11 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $51.1M.

sections.heading: Which agencies and markets dominate Granite Construction's federal work?
sections.body: Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer, obligating $537M to Granite Construction. Department of Defense obligated $13.4M and Department of Transportation obligated $11.7M. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest market for Granite Construction at $537M, followed by Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction at $13.1M and Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction at $11.8M.
